### Observed differences

- In the later window, A19, A20 and A25 occur much later in the case: their mean event position moves from about 0.33 to about 0.59–0.61 of the case length, while A26 and A27 stay at essentially the same position (about 0.35 to 0.33, and 0.58 to 0.56). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]
- The order relative to the stable activities reverses: before, A19, A20 or A25 preceded A26 and A27 in about 24–38 in 100 cases and followed them in at most about 1 in 200; in the later window they follow A26/A27 in about 29–37 in 100 cases and precede them in about 1 in 200. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL006, REL007]
- Routing changes accordingly: before, about 92–99 in 100 outgoing transitions of A19, A20 and A25 led to A26; in the later window about 93–99 in 100 lead to A28 or A32 instead. A45, which previously fed the block (about 94 in 100 transitions to A19/A20/A25), now leads directly to A26 (about 94 in 100). A28 now hands over to A19/A20/A25 in about 53 in 100 transitions (before: A32 about 99 in 100), and A27 does so in about 43 in 100 (before: A28 about 97 in 100). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]
- Step distances match this: A27 reaches A32 in 3 steps in about 93 in 100 later cases (2 steps in about 97 in 100 before), and A45 reaches A26 in 1 step in about 94 in 100 later cases (2 steps before). [LAG006, LAG011]
- Participation also shifts: A24 appears in about 58 in 100 later traces versus about 43 before; within the moving block, A20 rises from about 25 to about 38 in 100 cases while A19 and A25 fall to about 33 and 30; the three remain nearly mutually exclusive, their shares summing to about 100 in 100 cases in both windows. [OCC001, POS001, POS002, POS003, REL001, REL003, REL006, POS004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the alternative block A19/A20/A25 — of which about one executes per case — was relocated from before A26 (between A45 and A26) to the segment between A27/A28 and A32, with A26, A27, A28 and A32 keeping their positions and A45 now connecting straight to A26. The support is direct and consistent across indicator families: the order relative to A26/A27 reverses, only the block activities shift later (by roughly a quarter of the case length), successors change at A45, A19/A20/A25, A27 and A28, and step distances move as expected if the block is removed from before A26 and inserted before A32. The 31 items are about fifty times the 0.62 expected for an unchanged process, and the old arrangement is nearly absent afterwards (A19 before A26 in about 1 in 200 later cases), which a rare-variant explanation struggles to cover — while noting that the items largely describe one underlying difference rather than independent confirmations. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL006, REL007, POS001, POS002, POS003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, LAG006, LAG011]

Limitations: the block's exact insertion point is mixed — in the later window A27 hands to A28 in about 54 in 100 transitions and to the block in about 43, and A28 hands to A32 in about 45 and to the block in about 53 — so its precise placement relative to A28 is uncertain. A24's higher participation (about 43 to 58 in 100 traces) is a single occurrence signal with no relational evidence linking it to the relocation. Shifts in which alternative is chosen (A20 up, A19 and A25 down) and some lag profiles rest on few observations (some lag items have only 1–2 supporting pairs in one window), so sampling differences in variant frequencies between the two 200-trace windows cannot be ruled out for those components. [OCC001, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG005, LAG009, LAG010, POS001, POS002, POS003]
